name: Saudi Arabia
genZNote: Saudi Arabia holds Islam's two holiest cities (Mecca and Medina) and roughly a sixth of the world's proven oil reserves — one nation quietly running both the religious centre of gravity for over a billion Muslims and a huge chunk of the global energy market.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Occupies most of the Arabian Peninsula in West Asia, bordered by Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain (via causeway), the UAE, Oman, and Yemen.
Dominated by vast desert terrain, including the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter), one of the largest continuous sand deserts in the world.
Home to Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, making it the destination for the annual Hajj pilgrimage.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic is the official language; Islam (specifically its role as custodian of Islam's holiest sites) is central to national identity and legal/social life.
Traditional Bedouin heritage, hospitality customs, and tribal social structures remain culturally significant alongside rapid modernisation.
Recent social reforms under 'Vision 2030' have expanded women's rights (including the right to drive, from 2018) and opened up entertainment and tourism sectors.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: An absolute monarchy ruled by the House of Saud, with the King as both head of state and head of government; there is no elected national legislature, though a royally-appointed Consultative Assembly (Shura Council) advises on policy.
Governed under Islamic law (Sharia) as its legal framework, with the Quran and Sunnah serving as the country's constitution.
Pursuing an ambitious economic and social transformation plan, 'Vision 2030', to diversify away from oil dependence.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Investing heavily in advanced healthcare infrastructure and biotechnology as part of Vision 2030 economic diversification.
Hosts King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), a major research university attracting international scientific talent.
Developing large-scale renewable energy and green hydrogen projects (e.g., NEOM) alongside its traditional oil and gas sector.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G20 member and the de facto leader of OPEC, giving it major influence over global oil markets and prices.
A key strategic partner of the United States in the Middle East, while also expanding relations with China, Russia, and other major powers.
Plays a central diplomatic role in the Islamic world as custodian of Mecca and Medina and a founding member of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Saudi Arabia share a 'Strategic Partnership', with Saudi Arabia being one of India's top crude oil suppliers and a major source of remittances from the large Indian expatriate workforce.
Saudi Arabia hosts millions of Indian workers, making the bilateral labour and remittance relationship one of India's most significant globally.
Growing investment ties, with Saudi sovereign wealth funds investing in Indian infrastructure and technology sectors, alongside cooperation on counter-terrorism and defence.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: The world's largest oil exporter historically, with petroleum accounting for the majority of government revenue and exports, though Vision 2030 aims to diversify this.
Aramco, the state oil company, is one of the world's most valuable and highest-revenue companies.
Growing investment in tourism, entertainment, mega-projects (like NEOM), and renewable energy as part of economic diversification.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being home to Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and hosting the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
Holding some of the world's largest proven oil reserves and leading OPEC.
Vision 2030 — an ambitious economic and social reform and diversification programme.
Being a major destination for the large Indian expatriate workforce.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy on the Arabian Peninsula, custodian of Islam's holiest sites and a leading global oil power pursuing Vision 2030 diversification.
keyFacts: Absolute monarchy ruled by the House of Saud; governed under Islamic law.
Home to Mecca and Medina, Islam's two holiest cities.
Leading OPEC member and historically the world's largest oil exporter.
commonConfusion: Saudi Arabia has a Shura Council for consultation, but it is appointed, not elected — the country has no elected national legislature.

highYieldFacts: Saudi Arabia: absolute monarchy, capital Riyadh, custodian of Mecca and Medina.
Leading OPEC member; historically world's top oil exporter.
India-Saudi: major crude oil supplier to India and top source of remittances via large Indian expatriate workforce.
commonTraps: Assuming Saudi Arabia has an elected parliament — the Shura Council is appointed, not elected.
Confusing OPEC leadership influence with sole control of global oil prices — many other factors and producers matter too.
mustRemember: Saudi Arabia: absolute monarchy, Mecca/Medina custodian, OPEC leader, key India oil/remittance partner via Vision 2030 reforms.
